findings.title: descend(movable=...) does not confine moves to the movable set: reach jumps move other slot and column coordinates
findings.detail: _Space.neighbours limits the ±step singles to `idx`, but it always adds every reach jump from twin._walk_candidates(reach=True), whichever parameters are movable. Those jumps rewrite slot u-ends and column outer edges. So `descend(spec, p, score, movable=[...])` can change parameters the caller excluded. The author's own test `test_descend_stops_at_a_non_trivial_local_optimum` says 'One movable parameter', which the code does not guarantee. That test passes only because its score depends on slot0_v0, which no jump touches. The tie-order test (movable=[ia, ib]) has the same exposure. local_search itself is not affected, because its idx always holds every column and slot, and dies_fixed is still respected because no jump moves a die row. Planned uses that pass movable=None (the proxy rule, nulls over the search's parameters) are also unaffected. A caller who restricts `movable`, for example a null meant to move only some parameters, would silently get a larger move set.
findings.evidence: Scratch run on halfbridge_housing_spec(3, wires_per_die=1), generate(seed 21, reach=True): descend(movable=['land_HS'], score = -L1 distance of the col/slot coords from the start, step_limit=5) took moves ['slot0_free>limit', 'slot2_attach>col_outer', 'slot1_attach>limit', 'slot3_attach>limit', 'slot0_attach>col_inner'] and changed ['slot0_u0','slot0_u1','slot1_u0','slot2_u1','slot3_u0']. land_HS, the only movable parameter, did not move.
findings.suggested_check: Keep a jump only if the coordinate it changes is in idx, and add a test where the score rewards moving a non-movable column or slot coordinate.

findings.title: budget=0 or shortlist=0 fails with an opaque error
findings.detail: LocalConfig does not validate its fields. With budget=0, evaluate(seed) raises _Budget before anything is visited, the shortlist is empty, and `min(range(0))` raises a bare ValueError. shortlist=0 fails the same way. The default config is unaffected.
findings.evidence: Scratch run: local_search(..., LocalConfig(budget=0)) raised `ValueError min() iterable argument is empty`.
findings.suggested_check: Validate budget >= 1 and shortlist >= 1 in LocalConfig.__post_init__.

findings.title: Best-improvement over the full neighbourhood costs about 80 L1 evaluations per accepted step
findings.detail: Each iteration evaluates every valid single move, every reach jump and 12 joint moves before taking one step. On the 70x40 housing with an unrelated seed, 400 evaluations bought 5 steps (80 evaluations per step), so the default budget of 2000 buys roughly 25 accepted moves. This is a design and configuration choice, not a bug. Whether it is enough to recover R_D of 1.25-1.60 degradations within E011's frozen budget is exactly what E011 will measure; F4's 'stopped at budget' report covers it.
findings.evidence: Scratch run: budget=400 gave steps=5, perturbations=0, last_improve_eval=371, stop_reason=budget; Manhattan distance to the target went from 216.125 to 209.625.
findings.suggested_check: Before freezing E011's budget, run development draws at the intended budget and report steps and improving_last10.

findings.title: Checkpoint keys are not namespaced by solver or score
findings.detail: Store keys are `local:{fp}:l1` and `local:{fp}:lsub` in workdir/local_checkpoint.jsonl. If a workdir is reused with a different injected l1 (for example a blind null scorer passed as l1) or a different l_sub, the stored values are returned silently. This is safe only if every run with different solvers gets its own workdir. The docstring does not state that requirement.
findings.evidence: local.py lines 326 and 385: the key contains only the fingerprint and the kind.
findings.suggested_check: Document one workdir per solver pair, or add a solver tag to the key namespace.

findings.title: Landing lines step by 0.5 mm although the reach domain puts them on the 0.125 mm grid
findings.detail: _step_of gives the 0.125 mm step only to foot_* parameters. land_HS and land_LS step by 0.5 mm, and the reach-mode in_domain accepts them on the 0.125 mm grid. The module docstring documents this. The effective landing point (land + foot land_dv, with land_dv on the 0.125 mm grid within ±0.375 mm) is still reachable on the fine grid, so the effect is small. It is a limit on the objective's phrase 'move set ranges over the whole DRC-feasible domain'.
findings.evidence: derivative.py line 1243: `_ong(ln, FOOT_GRID_MM if rch else DESIGN_GRID_MM)`; local.py _step_of.

independent_checks_performed: Ran the three definition-of-done commands: test_local_search.py gave 16 passed; tests/unit/optimize not-slow gave 57 passed and 1 deselected; ruff check passed.

Read derivative.in_domain, _ong, Params.NAMES and from_vector, twin._walk_candidates and Layout.fingerprint. Checked that ±0.5 and ±0.125 updates on grid values are exact in binary and that fingerprints quantize to 1 nm, so float drift does not split visited layouts or double-count the budget.
Adversarial scratch run: descend with movable=['land_HS'] and a score that rewards moving columns and slots. Confirmed that reach jumps move 5 slot coordinates that were not movable.
Edge case: local_search with LocalConfig(budget=0) raises an opaque ValueError.
Cost check: at budget 400 on the housing spec, 80 L1 evaluations per accepted step (5 steps).
Recomputed the Spearman closed form in the test by hand: d^2 sum = 2, so 1 - 12/60 = 0.8, which is correct. Checked that the tie-averaging rank implementation matches the standard definition.

Checked the budget accounting logic by hand: _Budget is raised before a new fingerprint is solved, store hits still count, and visited layouts cost nothing. This agrees with the exact-budget and resume tests, which recompute the shortlist independently from the visited vectors.
caveats: The restricted `movable` argument of descend is unreliable: reach jumps always run and can move any slot end or column outer edge. Use descend only with movable=None (optionally dies_fixed=True), which is what the proxy rule and the full-parameter nulls need, until the jumps are filtered to idx.

local_search is checked only with synthetic injected solvers (parameter-space Manhattan distance, which separates by parameter and is easy for single-parameter descent) and a 2R stand-in. Nothing here shows that it recovers planted headroom with the real L1 or l2_layout; that is E011's job.

At the default budget of 2000 the search makes roughly 25 accepted moves (about 80 evaluations per step measured on the housing spec). Whether that suffices for R_D 1.25-1.60 degradations is untested here.
Each run that uses a different l1 or l_sub needs its own workdir, because checkpoint keys hold only the fingerprint and the kind.

I could not get the time-and-memory measurement of a full default-budget run (2000) to run in this session: the command was refused. Memory growth of the unbounded _Space.cache was therefore not measured.
